items.headline: Economy adds 165,000 jobs as unemployment dips to 4.1%
items.summary: U.S. employers added 165,000 jobs in October, more than forecasters expected, and the unemployment rate fell to 4.1%. PBS reports that inflation continues to erode Americans' spending power.

items.headline: Newsom commutes every death sentence in California
items.summary: California Gov. Gavin Newsom commuted all of the state's death sentences, moving the condemned to life in prison without parole. TIME's explainer looks at the reactions and the legal questions the move raises.

items.headline: Harmeet Dhillon resigns as Justice Department civil rights chief
items.summary: Harmeet Dhillon resigned as head of the Justice Department's Civil Rights Division. Her tenure brought sweeping changes to the division that drew both support and criticism.

items.headline: Nithya Raman unseats Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass
items.summary: Democratic socialist Nithya Raman defeated incumbent Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass in an upset. PBS describes the result as a generational shift in the city's politics.

items.headline: Zelenskyy presses for 'clear' postwar security guarantees
items.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy called for concrete, documented guarantees of Ukraine's security once the war ends. He made the case as the fighting continues to take a heavy toll on the country.

items.headline: EU accuses TikTok of breaking its digital rules
items.summary: The European Union's executive arm said TikTok violated the bloc's digital rules. It said the platform must redesign its "For You" feed to give users more control over opting out of certain content.

items.headline: Macao jails ex-lawmaker in first national security case
items.summary: Former Macao legislator Au Kam San was sentenced to 12.5 years in prison. His was the first publicly known prosecution under the territory's national security law, enacted in 2009.

items.headline: Europe's far-right leaders distance themselves from Trump
items.summary: Far-right leaders in Europe are backing away from President Trump after Republican losses in the U.S. midterm elections. TIME reports on how the results are reshaping those political ties.

items.headline: Japan's emptying countryside is losing its wildlife
items.summary: Rural depopulation in Japan is coinciding with a decline in wildlife. The losses extend to areas where farmland has been abandoned.

items.headline: Gold prices slide despite economic uncertainty
items.summary: Gold has fallen from nearly $5,600 in January to below $4,000, even though it usually gains in uncertain times. NPR's Planet Money examines why.

digest.overview:
President Trump named Stephen Miller as White House chief of staff starting Monday, replacing Susie Wiles. Trump also confirmed what he called minor U.S. strikes on Iranian air defenses on Qeshm Island, the first since the midterms, and the U.S. offered up to $20 million for information on Iran's nuclear program. Employers added 165,000 jobs in October and unemployment fell to 4.1%, though inflation is still eroding spending power. In Alaska, Democrat Mary Peltola leads Sen. Dan Sullivan by about 600 votes, while in Mississippi Sen. Hyde-Smith's lawyers demanded that counties preserve affidavit ballots as her Democratic challenger holds a narrow lead. California Gov. Gavin Newsom commuted all 548 of the state's death sentences. Harmeet Dhillon resigned as head of the Justice Department's Civil Rights Division, and democratic socialist Nithya Raman unseated Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass.

Abroad, Russian missiles struck Kyiv early Saturday, injuring at least five and cutting power and water, ahead of U.S.-brokered talks with Russia set for Tuesday in Abu Dhabi. A senior North Korean party envoy met top Chinese officials in Beijing, and the U.N. urged both Koreas to restore military hotlines amid DMZ tensions. China raised serious concerns over U.S. restrictions in a call with Treasury Secretary Bessent and vowed to answer new U.S. sanctions on two Chinese firms. Japan unveiled an emergency cybersecurity package after a wave of attacks, and a former Macao lawmaker got 12.5 years in the territory's first national security case. Paraguay's Senate removed President Santiago Peña over a bank collapse, and New Zealand's election was too close to call on early counts.

home.overview:
Luka Dončić scored a season-high 53 as the Lakers rallied past Portland 124–118 on a nine-game NBA Cup night, while LeBron James managed 8 points in his return to Cleveland as the Cavaliers routed Philadelphia 119–95. Jayson Tatum had 34 in Boston's 119–80 rout of Charlotte and Victor Wembanyama posted 30 and 14 in San Antonio's win at Sacramento; Golden State's Kristaps Porziņģis is stepping away for health reasons. Seven games are on tonight, starting with Nuggets–Pacers in Mexico City. In the NFL, Baltimore's Jacoby Brissett trade became official ahead of Tuesday's deadline, Shedeur Sanders starts for Cleveland, and Sunday opens with Bengals–Falcons in Madrid.

Thierno Barry scored twice as Everton came from behind to beat Coventry 3–1 and move fifth in the Premier League, and Leicester survived a scare to win 4–2 at sixth-tier Oxford City in the FA Cup. Hamburg and Toulouse both won 3–1 on Friday. Today brings Nottingham Forest v Man City and MLS Decision Day, where Nashville can set a points record; Sunday has Atlético v Barcelona and Crystal Palace v Liverpool. In K League 2, wins for Suwon FC and Seoul E-Land delayed Suwon Samsung's promotion. In the KBO, Samsung beat KT Wiz 5–1 and 10–5 in Daegu for a 3–1 Korean Series lead and can clinch in Sunday's Game 5.

brief: Samsung beat KT Wiz 5–1 in Game 3 in Daegu on Friday as Ariel Jurado allowed one run over seven innings and Koo Ja-wook hit a two-run triple.
Samsung then won Game 4 10–5 on Saturday to take a 3–1 series lead, with Park Seung-kyu driving in three runs and Lee Jae-hee throwing 2⅔ perfect innings in relief.
Samsung rested injured catcher Kang Min-ho for Game 4, and his replacement, Kim Do-hwan, hit a bases-clearing double in the first.
KT manager Lee Kang-chul publicly called on slugger Ahn Hyun-min to produce more as the Wiz fell behind.
Samsung can clinch the title in Game 5 at 2 p.m. Sunday in Daegu, with homegrown ace Won Tae-in facing KT's Davis Daniel; Games 6 and 7, if needed, would be in Suwon next Tuesday and Wednesday.
